title: Tanzania; Tsunami Alert Fear Grips Dar es Salaam
article_text:
Tanzania; Tsunami Alert Fear Grips Dar es Salaam
Africa News
April 12, 2012 Thursday


Copyright 2012 AllAfrica, Inc.
Length: 474 words
Byline: Tanzania Daily News (Dar es Salaam)
Body


RESIDENTS in Dar es Salaam and other areas along the country's Indian Ocean coastline went on alert yesterday after a powerful 8.6 magnitude earthquake struck off Indonesia's coast on Wednesday.
The quake prompted the Tanzania Meteorological Agency (TMA) to issue an alert, saying it expected waves of up to 1.5 metres to hit the country's coastline between 6pm and 7pm.
According to the agency, there was likelihood of huge waves in the Indian Ocean, advising fishermen and all sea-going vessels to keep off the sea.
TMA warned beach goers, fishermen and other people running activities along the beaches or residing near them, especially in Mtwara Region to temporarily evacuate.
TMA's Head of Research and Applied Meteorology Dr Emmanuel Mpeta told the 'Daily News' yesterday that coastal areas particularly Mtwara, Dar es Salaam, Zanzibar and Tanga were likely to be struck by the disastrous phenomenon. He said TMA was analyzing available data to determine potential for
tsunami occurrence in the country's territorial waters but cautioned people conducting activities around beach areas to vacate for their safety.
"It is predicted that Tanzania's coastal areas particularly Mtwara, are likely to be affected by the earthquake waves, coming from Madagascar Island, moving at the 8.6cm magnitude in the Richter scale that usually form a moderate tsunami," he explained.
Dr Mpeta said areas likely to be affected should be on the alert between 6pm and 7pm yesterday, while the quake would slowly disappear after about two to three hours. "We are monitoring the situation and will keep on providing updates," the agency said.
Panic gripped residents in the City centre as news of the looming tsunami circulated fast on the internet. In some offices workers reportedly closed business early than usual and rushed home.
A heavy downpour that pounded the city for hours complicated transport and communication services.
Internet and mobile phone services were interrupted temporarily while there was a heavy traffic jam in the city centre. Dr Mpeta, however, said people staying in high rise buildings were not likely to be affected although it was advised they better took maximum precautions.
The Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office responsible for Policy, Coordination and Parliamentary Affairs, Mr William Lukuvi, confirmed he was aware of the latest development from TMA and promised to issue more relevant information should need arise.
The tsunami alert is reminiscent of a devastating scenario in December 2004 when more than 230,000 people, nearly three-quarters of them in Indonesia's Aceh province died.
More than 10 people died in Tanzania. Other countries where the tsunami warning has been issued include India, Sri Lanka, Australia, Myanmar, Thailand, Maldives, British Indian Territories, Malaysia, Mauritius, Reunion and Seychelles.
